name: Headway
tagline: Subscription app that serves 15-minute summaries of popular nonfiction books, plus daily-streak gamification and audio narration.

pricing.basis: annual subscription, discounted from a headline monthly rate
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Headway prices vary heavily by onboarding funnel and promo, so treat any single number as noise.

verdictSummary: The software here is trivial: a list of cards, a reader view, an audio player, a streak counter. The product is the library, roughly a thousand-plus editorially condensed nonfiction titles, each one written, fact-checked, narrated, and legally cleared enough to sell. An agent can absolutely build you a summarizer, but it can only summarize books you already have, which is the opposite of the reason people subscribe: they want the summary instead of the book. What you can one-shot is a personal digest tool for your own library, which is genuinely useful and genuinely not Headway. Also worth noting that the entire category exists to make you feel like you read something, and a local tool with no streak animation removes most of the mechanism that keeps you coming back.
coreLoopDIY: Point it at EPUBs and PDFs you own, get chapter-level key-insight summaries plus a TTS audio version and a spaced-repetition card deck, all stored locally.
requirements: An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI) in .env
EPUB or PDF files you actually own
Optional TTS API key or a local TTS binary for audio
whatYouLose: The catalog: you can only summarize what you already own, and if you owned and read it you did not need the summary
Professional narration and a real mobile app with offline downloads and background audio
Editorial quality control, so your summaries are as reliable as whatever the model hallucinated at 2am
Streaks, daily challenges, and the whole behavioral scaffolding that makes people finish anything
Curation: someone deciding which 1,200 books are worth condensing and in what order
moatNotes: Condensed-book publishing sits in an odd legal zone that only survives with lawyers, staff writers, and licensing relationships. That is expensive and boring, which is exactly what makes it a moat.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the money buys content that does not exist yet, not features. Someone read the book, argued about what mattered, wrote it into eight crisp screens, recorded it, and shipped it to your phone with an audio player that survives a subway ride. A personal build inverts the value: it can only compress things you already possess. Add to that the fact that most subscribers are buying a habit rather than a tool, and the streaks, notifications, and polished onboarding funnel are load-bearing product, not decoration.
notes: The reader app is an afternoon; the library is a publishing company. The moat is content rights plus a thousand professionally written and narrated summaries you cannot legally or practically reproduce.
prompt:
Build "Distill", a local-only tool that turns ebooks I own into short key-insight summaries with optional audio. No accounts, no cloud storage, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI, Jinja2 templates, htmx for interactivity, plain CSS. No React.
- SQLite via sqlite3 stdlib, single file data/distill.db.
- ebooklib + BeautifulSoup for EPUB text, pypdf for PDF text.
- Anthropic API via the official SDK. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY read from .env with python-dotenv. Never hardcode keys.

Features in scope:
1. CLI: `python -m distill ingest path/to/book.epub` extracts title, author, and chapter-level plain text into SQLite.
2. Chunk chapters to fit context, then summarize in two passes: per-chapter key insights (3 to 6 bullets each, max 40 words per bullet), then a whole-book summary of 8 to 12 numbered insights plus a 2-sentence "who should read the full book" note. Cache every LLM call by content hash so re-runs cost nothing.
3. Web UI at localhost:8000: library grid, book detail page showing the numbered insights, a per-chapter accordion, and a "source snippet" toggle that shows the extracted text each insight came from so I can check for hallucination.
4. Flashcards: generate one question/answer card per top-level insight, store them, and expose a /review page with basic SM-2 spaced repetition (again / hard / good / easy).
5. Optional audio: `python -m distill audio <book_id>` writes an MP3 of the whole-book summary using pyttsx3 if no TTS key is set. Expose it in the UI with an HTML5 audio tag.
6. Export: markdown file per book into exports/.

Out of scope, do not build: any book catalog or downloader, piracy or scraping of book text, user auth, mobile apps, payment, streaks, push notifications.

Deliverables: working code, requirements.txt, .env.example, and a README that states plainly that this only works on files the user legally owns and that summaries are model-generated and may be wrong. Include pytest coverage for the EPUB parser and the SM-2 scheduler. Make `python -m distill ingest sample.epub && uvicorn distill.app:app` work from a clean checkout.
